explanation: The team entered the two-man and four-man events in Canada. Their four-man sled crashed during the competition, and the crew walked beside it to the finish line.

claims.text: Jamaica's bobsleigh team made its Olympic debut at the 1988 Winter Olympics in Calgary.
Jamaica did not compete in Olympic bobsleigh at Sarajevo 1984, and Albertville 1992 and Lillehammer 1994 came after its debut.
At Calgary 1988 Jamaica entered both the two-man and the four-man bobsleigh events.
Jamaica's four-man sled crashed at Calgary, and the crew walked alongside it to the finish.
The 1993 film Cool Runnings was loosely based on the Jamaican bobsleigh team.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: The crash happened on the third run of the four-man event, and the team then walked beside the sled rather than carrying it. [...] The team walked alongside the bobsleigh while support staff pushed it to the end of the track. [...] Olympics.com says the film is inaccurate on this point. The team did not pick up the sleigh and carry it over the line. Instead, they walked next to it.

editor.reason: Second pass, after tiebreak fc-tbp3t. A pass, B revise, T pass (§9.7). B's revise was its doubt on c4 (the crew walked beside the crashed sled to the finish). T's search (Olympics.com, the IOC's site, named in its summary, and Wikipedia; counted at Tier B) says the four-man sled crashed on its third run and the team walked alongside it to the end of the track rather than carrying it, as the film shows. So c4, which needed the tiebreak, has external evidence, and B's fix is rejected on it. A and B confirmed high-risk c1, c2, c3 and c5 directly at certain (memo §18).
